policy.bounded_partial: A declared subset/proxy fit is executable from primary rows, but missing source inputs or protocol details prevent an authoritative full-fit comparison.
policy.not_refittable: The primary source supplies no direct row-level observations, or the necessary reduction/calibration is not executable.
policy.parity: Every fitted parameter agrees within combined 2-sigma and also meets the parameter-specific numerical similarity threshold. The Sakai 2018 rhenium audit explicitly accepts numerical parity within reported parameter error widths, with comparable refit standard errors; its source confidence convention remains unknown.
policy.parity_not_achieved: At least one fitted parameter is outside both the uncertainty and similarity criteria, or a dedicated partial-source audit cannot reproduce the published coefficient pair.
policy.reconstructed: A derived record is reproduced exactly from separately audited source components without optimizing composite coefficients. Any independent component refit and source-data validation are reported separately.
policy.similar: Every fitted parameter either agrees within combined 2-sigma or meets the documented parameter-specific similarity threshold.
policy.source_reconstruction: A coupled source-level calculation is executable, but omitted upstream observations or weights prevent independent recovery of the published EOS coefficients.

records.label: Shi et al. (2022), selected BM3-MGD corundum model 3
records.primary_data_finding: All 75 corundum P-T-V rows are bundled with every printed parenthetical uncertainty and their Pt-versus-NaCl pressure-calibrant grouping. The two horizontal table blocks are normalized without deduplication or inferred values.
records.source_notes: Published corundum model 3 selected in main Table 1 and Supporting Information Table S3: a third-order Birch-Murnaghan 300 K reference isotherm plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The prose calls the cold term Murnaghan, but Equation 2 is algebraically BM3; fixed K0'=4 makes its cold curve numerically BM2. Equations 3-6 define Delta Pth=gamma/V [E_D(V,T)-E_D(V,300 K)], gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q, and theta=theta0 exp[-(gamma-gamma0)/q], with n=5 atoms per Al2O3 formula unit. V0=255.1 A^3 is the fixed conventional six-formula-unit hexagonal corundum cell from Lutterotti and Scardi (1990); K0, gamma0, and q were fitted, while K0', V0, theta0, Tr, and n were fixed. Main Table 1 reports K0=246(2) GPa for the selected model, whereas sensitivity Table 2 reports 246(1) GPa; the selected-table uncertainty is retained and the discrepancy is explicit. Table 2's 500 K and 800 K Debye-temperature trials are sensitivity fits, not additional preferred records. All 75 Table S1 observations are bundled: 59 are grouped under Pt pressures (including the fixed 0 GPa reference row) and 16 under NaCl pressures. The source does not state an uncertainty confidence convention or coefficient covariance matrix. An independent unweighted Peritheos fit of pressure residuals at all 75 printed V-T states, with the published fixed parameters, returns K0=246.3083 GPa, gamma0=1.35931, and q=0.800868; all reproduce the published coefficients within their reported uncertainties. The published curve has a 1.23305 GPa pressure RMSE and the refit has a 1.19139 GPa RMSE. Weighting by the tabulated coordinate uncertainties does not recover q, so the parity result is specifically identified as an unweighted pressure-residual reproduction rather than an undocumented reconstruction of the authors' weighting.

The official supplement defines T0=298 K, theta0=1425 K, n=5 atoms per B4C formula unit, gamma(V)=gamma0*(V/V0)^q, and theta(V)=theta0*exp[(gamma0-gamma(V))/q]. With a=1, the paper's generalized Tange relation reduces exactly to this integrated constant-q MGD model. The final article reports gamma0=0.8 fixed and q=2.1 varied. A Peritheos P-V-T errors-in-variables refit with gamma0 fixed gives q=1.050(519), so it does not independently recover q=2.1; details and the primary-data transcription are in docs/literature-reproductions.md. The average disordered R-3m structure is diffraction-ready and is reported stable over the experimental range.

records.source_notes: The paper calls this the Berman P-V-T fit. EosFit7 implements the Berman reference volume as the truncated quadratic V0(T)=V0*[1+alpha0*(T-Tr)+0.5*alpha1*(T-Tr)^2], with K0(T)=K0+dK0/dT*(T-Tr). EosFit7c varied alpha0=1.94(16)e-5 K^-1 and dK0/dT=-0.008(3) GPa/K while alpha1=0.0573e-8 K^-2 and the 300 K BM3 parameters were fixed. The article's displayed exponential-integral equation instead describes EosFit's Fei-style exact integration and is inconsistent with its Berman label. The implied BM3 K0''=-0.0166 GPa^-1 is derived rather than an independent parameter. Reproduction diagnostics compare both EosFit effective-variance and Peritheos errors-in-variables objectives.

records.source_notes: Preferred Vinet reference isotherm plus a constant-q Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure relative to 1000 K. The integrated Debye-temperature law follows equations 4-10 of Tange et al. (2009), which Kawai and Tsuchiya explicitly adopt; n=5 for one CaSiO3 formula unit. V0 is already one cubic Pm-3m conventional cell because Z=1. The input stresses came from LDA-PWSCF NVT FPMD on an 80-atom 2x2x1 tetragonal-supercell representation constrained to cubic metrics, with 50 Ry cutoff, a 2x2x2 k-point grid, 1 fs steps, 1 ps equilibration, and 5 ps production averages. Figure 1 reports a convergence benchmark near 15 GPa and 2000 K: the 2x2x2 sampling gives diagonal stresses 15.3, 15.5, and 15.2 GPa, compared with 16.0, 16.1, and 14.6 GPa at Gamma only; no volume is printed, so this is not an EOS-fit row. No parameter uncertainties or covariance are reported, so missing errors are null rather than zero. The alternate BM3 column is intentionally not added because this contribution is limited to one literature EOS record and the article plots and abstracts the Vinet result. The abstract's K0=203.95 GPa reproduces Table 1 (for example 184.42 GPa rounds to 184.5 GPa at V/V0=0.70 and 4000 K), whereas the PDF-extracted Table 2 value 203.5 GPa predicts 184.06 GPa; the benchmark-consistent abstract value is retained. No numerical 298 K fit dataset, weights, coefficient covariance, or confidence level for the Table I coefficient errors is published in the inspected article and supplement. The upper/lower isotherm rows describe separate envelope fits, not coefficient errors or independent 298 K observations. A refit of the published 298 K EOS is not possible with the current information. Fratanduono explicitly describes the Gruneisen prescription for reducing measured stress to the principal isentrope, but does not explicitly specify the Debye isentrope-to-298 K calculation used in our diagnostic. Applying Kraus (2016) Eq. (16), its Debye caloric model, and theta0=343.5 K is our inference, not a confirmed reproduction of the 2020 reduction. The 53 candidate points also use an unconfirmed graphical Hugoniot input and omit 46 higher-compression rows. Their 1.562 GPa RMS agreement with the published curve does not establish recovery of the original data, coefficient parity, or a superior EOS.

records.source_notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. records.label: Correa et al. (2008), logarithmic-moment double-Debye Helmholtz
records.primary_data_finding: All 57 diamond DFT-MD pressure markers in vector Figure 8 are bundled as plot-digitized checkpoints. The paper does not tabulate the upstream cold-energy grid, phonon DOS/moments, regression weights, or covariance needed to refit the published coefficients.
records.source_notes: Complete diamond free-energy branch from equations 2-18; the double-Debye weights conserve the logarithmic phonon moment theta_0 (equation 13). Table I volumes are per atom; the public API uses A^3 per eight-atom conventional diamond cell and converts internally to J bar^-1 mol^-1 of atoms. The Vinet term is a motionless-ion DFT-GGA cold curve. The authors state that its theoretical V0 is about 3% too large after zero-point and thermal effects and may need an application-specific density shift; Peritheos preserves the published value. The constant anharmonic coefficient changes caloric properties but contributes no pressure. Electronic excitations are neglected for insulating diamond as in the source. Factor-of-two source ambiguity: Correa equation 18 defines F_anh=-a*T^2 with a=3.8e-5 K^-1, whereas Benedict 2014 says it carries over the same correction but writes F_anh=-alpha*T^2/2 and tabulates alpha=3.79e-5 K^-1. This record follows Correa literally; in Benedict's normalization the equivalent coefficient would be alpha=2*a. The source reports no coefficient uncertainties or covariance.

records.source_notes: Complete equations 3-7 Helmholtz model, not a Vinet curve combined with a generic Mie-Gruneisen-Debye correction. Table I volumes are per atom; the public API uses A^3 per eight-atom conventional diamond cell and converts internally to J bar^-1 mol^-1 of atoms. The Vinet curve is the motionless-ion 0 K cold curve, so V0=5.7034 A^3/atom is not a 300 K zero-total-pressure reference volume. Factor-of-two source ambiguity: Benedict writes F_anh=-alpha*T^2/2 and tabulates alpha=3.79e-5 K^-1, while the Correa 2008 correction it claims to retain is F_anh=-a*T^2 with a=3.8e-5 K^-1. This record follows Benedict literally; matching Correa's anharmonic energy would require alpha approximately 2*a. The source reports no coefficient uncertainties or covariance.

records.source_notes: Anderson et al. Equation (29): the adopted 300 K BM3 curve KT0=166.65 GPa and K0'=5.4823 is combined with [0.00714-0.0115*ln(V0/V)]*(T-300) GPa. This is a staged literature synthesis, not a global P-V-T regression: Tables I-IV combine heat-capacity, expansivity, and ultrasonic data from distinct sources; low-temperature expansivities were graphically smoothed; several derived curves were fit separately; K0'=5.2-5.5 was selected by a thermodynamic-consistency diagnostic; and the final static K0 and K0' were adopted from Heinz and Jeanloz. V0=67.79 A^3 is converted from the paper's ambient density 19.30 g/cm^3 and atomic mass 196.967 g/mol for the four-atom fcc cell. Table I prints Cp=1.1288 in units of 0.1 J g^-1 K^-1 at 300 K, but Equation (4) and Table IV gamma=2.974 independently imply about 1.288; both the printed and reconstructed values are preserved in the supporting dataset. Table V covers V/V0=0.66-1 and 300-3000 K. The stored 0.001 GPa/K dK_dT_V error is the explicit propagated contribution reported for the near-identical K0'=5.5 calculation; the paper notes an additional unquantified contribution from K0' uncertainty. No global objective, complete covariance matrix, row weights, digitized low-temperature smoothing curve, or exact numerical-integration protocol is published.

records.source_notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

records.solver_message: Both `ftol` and `xtol` termination conditions are satisfied.
records.source_notes: Static-lattice GGA pseudopotential calculation for the named magnesite phase using a fully relaxed 30-atom MgCO3 cell (Z=6), with atomic positions and cell shape relaxed at nine volumes. The source reports the zero-pressure reference volume and an isothermal BM3 fit, but no finite-temperature or vibrational contribution; temperature_ref=0 K records that static electronic reference. The nine calculated states span -2.41596 to 207.419 GPa. Table 1 incorrectly labels both its energy and volume columns as per formula unit: its 160-295 A^3 volumes, stated V0=287.49 A^3, Figure 1 volume axis, and exact BM3 pressure reproduction establish the 30-atom conventional-cell basis; the energy rows likewise recover K0=98.921 GPa only when interpreted per 30-atom cell and give a factor-of-six error under the printed label. The parenthetical K0 and K0_prime errors are preserved, but the source states no confidence convention or covariance and gives no V0 uncertainty. The alternative K0_prime=4 fit, K0=111(1) GPa is not stored because the article calls it a poor second-order fit and does not use it in the subsequent analysis. The calculation finds no discontinuity within the sampled pressure range but explicitly cannot rule out reconstructive transitions with an energy barrier.

records.label: Yu et al. (2024), BM3-MGD
records.primary_data_finding: All 74 printed P-T-a-c-V rows and every parenthetical uncertainty are bundled in source order. The anomalous source-order row 5 is preserved verbatim: a=4.508 A and c=14.310 A imply 251.85 A^3, not the printed V=246.96 A^3 used by the EOS fit.
records.source_notes: Preferred thermal parameterization from Table 1: a 300 K third-order Birch-Murnaghan reference isotherm plus quasi-harmonic Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. Equations 7-8 specify gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q and theta=theta0*exp[-(gamma-gamma0)/q], which is Peritheos's integrated_gruneisen law, not the Fei et al. variable-exponent law used for the Pt calibrant. The source conventional-cell volumes are converted internally to molar volume using Z=6, while the public API remains in A^3 per conventional hexagonal cell. The paper also reports a separate high-temperature BM3 reference-state fit with alpha0, alpha1, and dK/dT; it is not represented here because the preferred MGD model is explicitly described as more reliable for extrapolation and is used in the downstream mantle calculations. The publication does not report the regression weights, residual definition, coefficient covariance, or confidence convention for parenthetical parameter errors. An independent unweighted pressure-residual refit is therefore a transparent reproduction diagnostic rather than a claim to duplicate the unpublished regression protocol.

records.label: Li et al. (2006), acoustic absolute-pressure BM3
records.objective: unweighted simultaneous VP and VS residuals in km/s
records.primary_data_finding: All 17 reported compression and decompression states are transcribed from the official publisher Table 1 file with volume ratio, density, P- and S-wave velocities, elastic moduli, calculated absolute pressure, and every printed one-standard-deviation uncertainty. The independently reported ambient density and velocities from Section 2 are retained as the acoustic-fit anchor. The density and velocity columns are the direct source-fit observations; the elastic moduli and calculated pressures are derived outputs and are excluded from coefficient refitting. The official Table 2 file was also checked; it contains the same current-study adiabatic coefficients plus earlier literature comparisons, not additional primary observations.
records.qualification: Direct reproduction of the source measurement-to-coefficient chain, not a pressure-volume refit: the preferred decompression density, VP, and VS rows plus the independently measured ambient anchor are fitted to the published third-order acoustic finite-strain equations. Equation 4 then maps the fitted adiabatic K0S and K0S-prime to the stored isothermal K0T and K0T-prime; paragraph 10's K0T-in-L2/M2 approximation accounts for the measured isothermal strains. The calculated Table 1 pressures are downstream BM3 outputs and are never used as observations. The source does not publish its exact weights, iterative adiabatic-foot correction, covariance, or propagated isothermal errors, so the unweighted rounded-table reconstruction is classified as numerically similar rather than strict parity.
records.selection: Section 2 ambient density/VP/VS anchor plus all ten Table 1 decompression-after-annealing density/VP/VS rows
records.source_notes: This is the paper's executable 300 K absolute-pressure scale, but it is not a direct volumetric BM3 fit to independent pressure-volume observations. It is directly reproducible through the source's actual measurement-to-coefficient chain: measured acoustic velocities and density are fitted with third-order finite-strain equations to obtain adiabatic moduli, Equation 4 converts the preferred decompression fit to isothermal K0T and K0T', and BM3 Equation 3 then calculates pressure from volume. Table 1 pressures are therefore downstream EOS outputs, not independent observations suitable for a conventional P-V refit. The source reports one-standard-deviation errors for V0 and the fitted adiabatic elastic quantities, but does not propagate the adopted thermodynamic constants into isothermal K0T/K0T' errors or publish covariance; those stored errors remain null rather than being inferred. This pressure-scale construction is distinct from the pressure-calibrant-dependent Speziale (2001), Dewaele (2000), and Jacobsen (2008) MgO records.

records.label: Holmes et al. (1989), theoretical 300 K Vinet scale
records.primary_data_finding: All seven new Pt shock experiments printed in Table III are bundled as qualification evidence. A separate source-derived checkpoint grid evaluates the complete published Equation (11) parameterization without treating generated curve values as independent fit observations. The numerical LMTO E0(V), P0(V), density-of-states, and 300 K fit grids are not published.
records.reason: Equation (11) and Table IV make the published 300 K Vinet curve exactly reconstructable, but the source does not tabulate its LMTO E0(V), P0(V), density-of-states, or 300 K fit grid. The bundled Table III rows are shock-Hugoniot qualification experiments and must not be fitted as a 300 K isotherm; the source-derived equation checkpoints are circular fit inputs. The underlying theoretical regression therefore remains not independently refittable.
records.source_notes: The 300 K pressure scale is Holmes et al.'s theoretical universal (Vinet) EOS, qualified against shock data to at least 10% in pressure. Equation (11) and Table IV give V0=101.9 bohr^3/atom, P_T=798.31 GPa, and eta=7.2119; the executable Vinet coefficients are the exact mappings K0=P_T/3 and K0'=1+eta/1.5. Table IV's separately printed B_T=266 GPa and B_T'=5.81 are rounded interpretations of the same curve. The approximate finite-temperature extension adds alpha*B_T*(T-300 K), with alpha=0.261e-4 K^-1 and rounded B_T=266 GPa, and is stated to be adequate below 2000 K. The 300 K isotherm itself is represented through 550 GPa; 32-660 GPa is the shock-Hugoniot range, not the static-isotherm validity range. The source publishes no numerical LMTO E0(V), P0(V), density-of-states, or 300 K fit grid, so the analytical curve is exactly reconstructable but its underlying theoretical fit is not independently refittable.

records.source_notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

records.source_notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

records.label: Wang et al. (2012), principal Vinet-MGD presentation
records.primary_data_finding: All 56 Table 1 observations are bundled with data identifiers, temperature, pressure, tetragonal lattice parameters, conventional-cell volume, simultaneous Au volume, and every printed parenthetical e.s.d. The publisher's supplement endpoint was unavailable to this audit client, so the transcription was verified against the complete official HTML rendering of Table 1.
records.source_notes: This is a thermal EOS, not a standalone room-temperature Vinet fit. Equations 1 and 4-8 add a Debye Mie-Gruneisen pressure increment relative to 300 K; with a=1, gamma(V)=gamma0*(V/V0)^b and theta(V)=theta0*exp[-gamma0*((V/V0)^b-1)/b]. The paper also reports an equally successful BM3-MGD alternative: V0=46.55 A^3 fixed, K0=294(2) GPa, K0'=4.85(12), theta0=1130(100) K, gamma0=1.66(7), a=1 fixed, and b=2.9(4). Vinet is retained as the single executable record from this paper because Figure 2 uses it and Tables 3-4 present its values first, with BM3 in parentheses; the authors state that the two fits agree within analytical uncertainty rather than explicitly designating a preferred model. The fixed V0 rounds the independently measured recovered-sample value 46.553(19) A^3; null in parameter_errors means it was not a fitted coefficient, not that the ambient measurement lacked uncertainty. Several measurements crossed the established stishovite-CaCl2-type boundary without transforming on the experimental timescale; the authors report that excluding them gives identical fit results, so the marginal P-T envelope is not a rectangular phase-stability claim.

records.source_notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.
